title: The Group Chat of Maple Street
premise: Felix Lockridge, a foster kid counting days until graduation, transfers to Hollow Creek High, a school built atop the flooded town of Old Maple. The legendary ghost of the school — the Maple Warden — begins slipping Felix handwritten notes in ink that appears only on paper, revealing that the town's founders bound something beneath the school with an annual 'Founding Fete' tradition, and that the binding is failing. When Felix's found family of outcasts — Priya, Marcus, and June — start receiving notes too, they discover the Warden is the drowned town's last guardian, and the Fete's ritual must be renewed by students descended from the founders, or the old town will rise and take the new one down. The climax forces Felix to choose between exposing the truth that would destroy the town's identity and completing the ritual with a sacrifice of their own name and memories; Felix offers their name to the ink, the Warden is freed, and the friends rebuild the tradition honestly — as remembrance instead of erasure — with Felix keeping only the group chat, where the Warden now types goodnight.
about_author: Elodie Delacroix is the pen name of a former night-shift librarian who swears the school she attended was built over something old. She writes stories about kids who find their people in the unlikeliest group chats.

chapters.title: Day One Hundred and Eighty-Three
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Felix arrives at Hollow Creek High mid-year, cataloging exits and keeping a countdown to graduation in a group chat they never post in. Emotional beat: armored loneliness. A tour guide mentions the Maple Warden legend and Felix laughs it off, but the flooded town beneath the school unsettles them more than they admit.

chapters.title: The Outcasts' Table
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Priya the archivist, Marcus the skeptic, and June the runaway-adjacent artist adopt Felix at lunch, pulling them into a real group chat: 'Maple Street Rejects.' Emotional beat: cautious warmth. Priya shows Felix a 1923 photo of the school's cornerstone, and the date is wrong — the school was built before the town it claims to honor.

chapters.title: Ink That Shouldn't Exist
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Felix finds a note in their locker: 'FELIX LOCKRIDGE. You count days. I count years.' The ink is wet but the paper dry, and it smells like pond water. Emotional beat: dread sharpening into curiosity. Security cameras show no one at the locker, and the handwriting matches signatures in the 1923 yearbook Priya digitized.

chapters.title: June's Drawings
chapters.summary: June's POV. June admits she's been drawing the Warden for months — a figure of reeds and lantern light — before ever hearing the legend, and last night her sketchbook filled with maps of streets that don't exist. Emotional beat: fear of being 'the weird one' again. The maps match Old Maple exactly, and one street is labeled Maple Street.

chapters.title: The Founding Fete
chapters.summary: Marcus's POV. Marcus, whose family helped found Hollow Creek, debunks everything — until he finds his great-grandfather's journal describing the Fete not as a festival but as a 'renewal of the seal,' performed by four founder-blooded students every fifty years. Emotional beat: the collapse of his skepticism. The last renewal was 1975. It's overdue.

chapters.title: What the Flood Took
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya unearths the truth: in 1923 the founders dammed the creek, drowned Old Maple, and built the school over it to 'keep the past quiet.' The Warden was a real person — the town's teacher, Elias Marsh, who refused to leave. Emotional beat: grief for erased people. The notes aren't hauntings; they're a plea from someone the town chose to forget.

chapters.title: Group Chat at 3 A.M.
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. The four convene over the chat and decide to renew the ritual before the seal fails — the school's foundations are cracking, and the pond behind the gym is rising. Emotional beat: found family solidifying into purpose. The Warden leaves a fifth note: 'Four names. Four bloodlines. I have three. Find the fourth.'

chapters.title: Bloodlines and Liars
chapters.summary: Marcus's POV. Marcus, Priya, and June each carry founder blood; Felix doesn't. Felix hides their hurt behind jokes while secretly researching whether the ritual needs a fourth at all — or a substitute. Emotional beat: the ache of being the outsider even inside the found family. The ink answers Felix privately: 'You were never meant to be fourth. You were meant to be the key.'

chapters.title: The Underneath
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Following the Warden's map, the four find a maintenance tunnel behind the boiler room leading down into drowned Old Maple — streets intact under black water, classroom desks still arranged. Emotional beat: vertigo and wonder. In the old schoolhouse, Elias's lantern still burns, and the water parts around them like it's making room.

chapters.title: Elias Marsh, Warden
chapters.summary: Elias's POV (a haunting interlude). Elias remembers drowning, remembers the founders' bargain — his vigil buys the town above another fifty years — and remembers every renewal, when four students renewed the seal and forgot everything after. Emotional beat: weary devotion. He has watched Felix for months because Felix, unbound by founder blood, is the first person who could end the cycle instead of repeating it.

chapters.title: The Price on the Page
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya deciphers the full ritual: renewal requires the four to surrender their memories of the past year — including each other. Emotional beat: horror. The 'tradition' that made the town is a machine that eats friendship to feed the seal. Priya refuses to forget the group chat, and the ink in her notebook starts bleeding through every page.

chapters.title: Cracks in the Ceiling
chapters.summary: Marcus's POV. The seal's failure accelerates: the gym floods, founder portraits weep ink, and the school board announces the Fete will proceed 'as always' — run by adults who don't know what it really does. Emotional beat: ticking-clock panic. Marcus realizes his own parents were renewed in 1975 and have no memory of the friends they made that year — including a name crossed out in the yearbook.

chapters.title: The Crossed-Out Name
chapters.summary: June's POV. June identifies the crossed-out name — Ada Voss, a student who refused to forget in 1975 and vanished. Her sketchbook now draws Ada's face unbidden. Emotional beat: righteous anger. Ada's final sketch shows a door under the pond, and June understands: refusing the ritual doesn't kill you, it keeps you — like Elias, like the Warden, like every guardian the town never thanked.

chapters.title: Loyalty vs. Truth
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. The group fractures: renew the seal and survive but forget each other, or expose the truth and risk the town rising. Marcus argues for renewal; June for exposure; Priya for a third option no one's found. Emotional beat: the found family's first real fight, in the group chat and in person. Felix, silent, rereads the Warden's first note and notices the postscript they missed: 'Ask me what I'd choose.'

chapters.title: Interview with a Ghost
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Alone in the underneath, Felix finally speaks to Elias. Elias confesses he's tired, that the founders tricked him into eternal vigilance, and that the seal doesn't need blood — it needs a freely given name, willingly surrendered, which no founder-blooded student has ever truly given. Emotional beat: devastating compassion. Elias asks Felix not to save him, but Felix has never once left a friend behind.

chapters.title: The Plan Nobody Likes
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya engineers the third option: at the Fete, they'll perform the ritual but redirect it — offering the founders' erased names, Old Maple's true history, back to the seal, trading truth instead of memory. Emotional beat: fragile hope. The ink responds across every paper in the school at once: 'The seal will take what is offered. Be certain what you offer is enough.'

chapters.title: Fete Day
chapters.summary: Marcus's POV. The whole town turns out for the Fete; the adults run the hollowed-out version of the ritual, and beneath the gym floor the water rises to meet it. Emotional beat: dread under confetti. The four slip away during the founding pageant, down the boiler tunnel, as the school's lights fail floor by floor above them.

chapters.title: The Renewal
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. In the drowned schoolhouse, the four attempt the redirected ritual — speaking the names of Old Maple's dead, the streets, the drowned — and the seal rejects it: it wants a living name, freely given. Emotional beat: the climax's terrible clarity. Felix steps forward and offers their own — the name they've resented, the identity they've been hiding behind, the countdown that defined them.

chapters.title: What Felix Lockridge Gave
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Felix's name dissolves into ink and light; the seal, fed by truth freely given instead of memory stolen, transforms — the flood recedes, and Elias's vigil ends. He passes his lantern to the four. Emotional beat: release after a century. Felix wakes on the pond bank remembering everything except their own name, and their three friends say it back to them, over and over, to keep it theirs.

chapters.title: The Town That Remembers
chapters.summary: June's POV. The aftermath: the Fete is rebuilt as a remembrance, Old Maple's history taught openly, Ada Voss's name restored to the yearbook. Emotional beat: bittersweet repair. June paints a mural of Maple Street in the cafeteria, and the town argues about it — which, Priya notes, is how you know a truth has finally taken root.

chapters.title: New Contact: Warden
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Felix, legally renamed and choosing 'Felix' anyway, starts a new countdown — days since, not days until. A new contact appears in the group chat: WARDEN, typing from somewhere under the water, no longer a prisoner but a neighbor. Emotional beat: joy with roots. Elias sends one message: 'You count days. So do I. Thank you for making them worth counting.'

chapters.title: The Group Chat of Maple Street
chapters.summary: All four POVs, interleaved chat logs and scenes. Graduation day: the four walk the stage, the mural behind them, the pond calm and clear for the first time in a century. Emotional beat: full-circle belonging. The final message in the chat, sent by all four at once and answered by the Warden with a single lantern emoji: 'We stayed.'
